dictionary.Face: Derived from the part name suffix: _front_, _side_, _back_, _top_, _bottom_.
dictionary.Main Armour Rating: Rating of the THICKEST structural plate on that face - what you have to defeat.
dictionary.Main Plate (mm): Nominal thickness of that plate. FLAT value, no angle.
dictionary.Main Plate Effective vs KE (mm): Nominal x genericArmorQuality. Against sabot and solid shot.
dictionary.Main Plate Effective vs HEAT (mm): Nominal x cumulativeArmorQuality. Against shaped charges.
dictionary.Weakest Spot Rating: Rating of the THINNEST plate on that face - where the hole is.
dictionary.Weakest Spot Part: The part name of that hole. Usually a vision port, hatch ring or periscope guard.
dictionary.Spread Main vs Weakest (mm): Main minus weakest. A big spread means the face is only as strong as where you do not aim.
dictionary.Base Armour Class: DamageParts.armorClass - the vehicle default that parts inherit when they do not override.
dictionary.Layered Armour: Yes when the vehicle has a composite, spaced or ERA part group. These are never rated.
dictionary.Has Screens: Side skirts or shields present. Affects shaped charges; not modelled in the rating.
dictionary.Rated: Whether this vehicle received face ratings at all, and why not if it did not.
dictionary.Armour Parts: Structural plates with a thickness, for this vehicle.
dictionary.Variable-Thickness Parts: How many of this vehicle's plates are geometric rather than flat. High counts mean the flat numbers describe less of the vehicle.
dictionary.Threat Sample Size: How many rounds that percentage was computed over. Below ~300 treat the rating as noisy.
dictionary.Armour Class: armorClass on the part, or the vehicle's base class when the part does not override it.
dictionary.KE Quality: genericArmorQuality - kinetic multiplier, from the part or inherited from its class.
dictionary.Effective Thickness Max (mm): armorEffectiveThicknessMax - engine cap on what this plate can present.
dictionary.Armour Through (mm): armorThrough - the depth a round must clear to pass the part.
dictionary.Variable Thickness: variableThickness - the real value is geometric, from the mesh. Never rated.
dictionary.Embedded: The plate sits inside another - a composite layer, not an exposed surface.
dictionary.Hidden In X-Ray: hidableInXrayViewer - not shown in the in-game X-ray view.
dictionary.Ricochet Angle (deg): From the armour class. Impacts beyond this angle can bounce.
dictionary.Threats Penetrating (%): Share of anti-tank rounds carried by vehicles within +/- 1.0 BR that beat this plate's effective thickness.
dictionary.Rating: See READ ME. Strong and Immune are never issued.
dictionary.Rating Note: Plain-English reason for the rating or the refusal.
dictionary.Module Type: Ammunition, Fuel, Crew or Engine / drive.
dictionary.Part Count: How many parts of that type. Ammunition counts individual shells, so it is large by design.
dictionary.Min Armour Around It (mm): Thinnest armour value recorded on any part of that module group.
dictionary.Faces Exposed: Which faces those parts sit behind, with counts.
dictionary.Tandem Precharge Quality: Multiplier against a tandem warhead's precursor charge. Relevant to ERA.
dictionary.Restrain Damage: How much the class dampens damage that gets through.

readme: !! READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING ANY NUMBER !!
Armour angle lives in the 3D mesh, not in the data files. Every thickness here is a FLAT PLATE value. A 45 mm plate at 60 degrees stops far more than 45 mm.
Sloped vehicles - T-34, Panther, IS-3 - are systematically UNDER-rated here. Flat-armour vehicles - Tiger, KV, most casemates - rate about right. The error runs one way.
This dataset can tell you where armour is thin. It CANNOT tell you where you are safe. That is why no plate is ever labelled Strong or Immune - see the rating scale below.
The ground ammunition dataset built earlier (war_thunder_ground_vehicles.xlsx)
1253 ground vehicles with a battle rating and a damage model.
38913 plates with a resolvable face. 99,923 armour parts exist in total; the rest are internal fittings, equipment boxes and bolt-on clutter and are not included.
5948 - five faces per vehicle where present.
4996 - ammunition, fuel, crew and engine, aggregated per vehicle. The raw parts number over 250,000 because every shell in a rack is its own entity.

Not to other vehicles' armour. For each plate, the dataset counts what fraction of anti-tank rounds carried by vehicles within +/- 1.0 BR beat that plate's effective thickness. Kinetic rounds are compared against Effective vs KE, chemical rounds against Effective vs HEAT.
That is the matchmaking spread. Uptiers are where you get killed, so the threat pool includes them. Threat pools run from 328 to 1,043 rounds depending on bracket.
95% or more of the threats at your BR beat this plate.
70 to 95% beat it. This is where you aim.
30 to 70%. Too close to call without angles. Not an answer - a flag to go look.
Under 30% beat the flat thickness. NO strong or immune label is issued, because without impact angle that would be a safety claim the data cannot support.
233 of 1253 vehicles carry composite, spaced or ERA groups and are not rated at all. Reason below.
The file flags the plate variableThickness; its real value is geometric.

T-80BVM's body_front_dm reads 80 mm. Rated naively that is Paper. The real frontal figure is several hundred millimetres once the composite stack and slope apply. A confident wrong label on a top-tier tank costs more trust than the whole feature earns.

t_80b_composite_armor carries genericArmorQuality 0.07 and cumulativeArmorQuality 0.30. Multiplying nominal thickness by that gives nonsense unless you also know the geometric depth of the stack, which is in the mesh.

The thinnest plate on a face is usually a vision port, hatch ring or periscope guard, not the armour. Rating a face on it calls every tank in the game paper. So each face reports BOTH: the main plate (thickest structural plate on that face) and the weakest spot, named.

Main plate answers 'what do I have to defeat'. Weakest spot answers 'where is the hole'. The Spread column shows how far apart they are - a big spread means the face is only as strong as where you do not aim.
Each plate carries genericArmorQuality (versus kinetic) and cumulativeArmorQuality (versus HEAT), either on the part itself or inherited from its armour class. Effective = nominal x quality.

T-80BVM's textolite layer is 35 mm nominal with KE quality 0.5 and HEAT quality 0.32 - it counts as 17.5 mm against a sabot and 11 mm against a shaped charge. Nominal thickness alone is misleading on any layered plate.
GAME values, not real-world values. BRs move every patch.
Penetration on the threat side is itself partly estimated. 1,992 full-calibre rounds rest on a scale factor fitted to 2 observations. That error compounds with the angle error, in the same direction.
Ratings sit on thresholds. A plate near 70% or 95% flips label with a small input change. The extremes are reliable; the middle is not.
ERA is detected by group name only. Its actual effect is not modelled here.
START HERE. One row per vehicle per face. Main plate rating plus the named weakest spot. Colour-coded.
One row per vehicle. Five face ratings, crew, hull HP, layered flag, part counts.
Every structural plate with thickness, class, quality multipliers, effective values and its own rating.
Ammunition, fuel, crew and engine per vehicle: how many parts, what armour surrounds them, which faces they sit behind.
All 372 classes with their quality multipliers and ricochet behaviour.
Every column and its source key.
